In 2016, Downe, Finlayson, Tunçalp, and Metin Gülmezoglu conducted a systematic scoping review to identify the processes and outcomes of antenatal care that are important to healthy pregnant women. This study was published in BJOG and highlights the aspects of care that matter most to expectant mothers. 2. Fallon, Komninou, Bennett, Halford, and Harrold explored the emotional and practical experiences of mothers who formula-feed their infants. Their findings, published in Maternal and Child Nutrition in 2017, provide insights into the challenges and feelings associated with formula feeding. 3. Walters, Phan, and Mathisen analyzed the global economic impact of not breastfeeding using a novel tool. Their 2019 study in Health Policy and Planning emphasizes the financial and health-related costs of suboptimal breastfeeding practices. 4. Freitas and colleagues examined the sociodemographic profiles of mothers of children with congenital Zika syndrome. Their findings, published in Rev Panam Salud Publica in 2019, shed light on the characteristics of affected families. 5. Cames, Saher, Ayassou, Cournil, Meda, and Simondon investigated the acceptability and feasibility of infant-feeding options among HIV-infected mothers in Burkina Faso. Their 2010 study in Maternal and Child Nutrition focused on experiences within the WHO Kesho Bora PMTCT trial. 6. Rollins, Bhandari, Hajeehboy, Horton, Lutter, Martines, and colleagues discussed the importance of investing in breastfeeding and the necessary steps to improve breastfeeding practices. Their 2016 publication in The Lancet outlines the benefits and strategies for promoting breastfeeding globally. 7. Victora, Bahl, Barros, França, Horton, Krasevec, and colleagues reviewed the epidemiology, mechanisms, and lifelong effects of breastfeeding in the 21st century. Their comprehensive analysis was published in The Lancet in 2016. 8. De Oliveira Vianna, Lovero, De Oliveira, Fernandes, Dos Santos, and De Souza Lima studied children born to mothers with rashes during the Zika virus epidemic in Brazil. Their research, published in J Trop Pediatr in 2019, followed these children during the first 18 months of life. 9. Dos Santos, Soares, De Abranches, Da Costa, Moreira, and De Matos Fonseca examined the nutritional status and feeding practices of infants with microcephaly due to Zika virus exposure. Their findings were published in Nutr J in 2019. 10. Dos Santos, Soares, De Abranches, Da Costa, Gomes-Júnior, Fonseca, and colleagues analyzed the nutritional profiles of newborns with microcephaly and factors associated with worse outcomes. Their 2019 study in Clinics provides critical insights into the health challenges faced by these infants. 11. Soares, Abranches, Villela, Lara, Araújo, Nehab, and colleagues conducted a cohort study on Zika virus infection during pregnancy and its impact on infant growth and body composition in the first three months of life. Their findings were published in Sci Rep in 2019. 12. Cabral Cavalcanti, Costa Aguiar, De Oliveira Melo, Leite Cavalcanti, and D’Ávila investigated breastfeeding behaviors in Brazilian children with congenital Zika syndrome. Their study, published in Int J Dent in 2020, highlights the unique challenges faced by these families. 13. Cranston, Tiene, Nielsen-Saines, Vasconcelos, Pone, and colleagues explored the association between antenatal Zika virus exposure and anatomical and neurodevelopmental abnormalities in children. Their findings were published in JAMA Netw Open in 2020. 14. Falcao de Vale, Alves, and De Carvalho examined the daily reorganization of mothers caring for children with congenital Zika syndrome. Their 2020 study in Rev Gauch Enferm highlights the significant caregiving burden. 15. Menezes de Oliveira, De Melo, Mendes, Dos Santos Oliveira, Tavares, and Vaez studied oral and maxillofacial conditions, dietary aspects, and nutritional status in children with congenital Zika syndrome. Their findings were published in Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol in 2020. 16. De Sá, De Andrade, Nogueira, Lopes, Silva, and De Assis analyzed the needs of parents caring for children with Zika virus-induced microcephaly. Their 2017 study in Rev Brasil Promocao Saude provides insights into the support required by these families. 17. Vale, Cerqueira, Santos Jr., Black, and Carvalho explored families’ experiences and emotions surrounding the diagnosis of Zika-related microcephaly. Their findings were published in Nurs Inquiry in 2019. 18. Campos, De Sousa, Teixeira, Araújo, and Sousa examined the challenges and perspectives of mothers of children with microcephaly caused by the Zika virus. Their 2018 study in Rev Rede Enferm Nordeste highlights the difficulties faced by these families. 19. Da Silva Rodrigues Felix and De Farias studied the family dynamics and fathers’ perceptions of their children’s disabilities due to microcephaly. Their findings were published in Cadernos Saude Publica in 2018. 20. Scott, Lira, Matos, Souza, Silva, and Quadros analyzed therapeutic itineraries, care practices, and maternal perceptions of motherhood and childhood in the context of Zika. Their 2018 study in Interface Comunicacao Saude Educacao provides a sociocultural perspective. 21. Santos, Prado, Silva, Cardoso, and Oliveira examined the role of mothers in promoting the health of their children with microcephaly. Their findings were published in Rev Escola Enfermagem USP in 2019. 22. Cartwright and Boath conducted a qualitative study on the experiences of mothers feeding infants with Down’s syndrome. Their 2018 research in J Neonatal Nurs highlights the challenges and adaptations required. 23. Swift and Scholten explored parental experiences of infant feeding difficulties and family relationships in neonatal units. Their 2010 study in J Clin Nurs provides insights into the emotional and practical challenges faced by families. 24. Wieczorkiewicz and De Souza studied the breastfeeding process among mothers of children with Down’s syndrome. Their findings were published in Cogitare Enfermagem in 2009. 25. Donkor, Lee, Lelijveld, Adams, Baltussen, and Nyante investigated caregiver experiences and community-based training to improve the nutritional status of children with cerebral palsy in Ghana. Their 2018 study in Food Sci Nutr highlights the benefits of targeted interventions. 26. Morrow, Quine, and Craig examined health professionals’ perceptions of feeding-related quality of life in children with quadriplegic cerebral palsy. Their findings were published in Child Care Health Dev in 2007. 27. Barros da Silva, Barbieri-Figueiredo, and Van Riper explored the breastfeeding experiences of mothers of children with Down’s syndrome. Their 2018 study in Compr Child Adolesc Nurs provides a detailed account of these mothers’ journeys. 28. Adams, Khan, Begum, Wirz, Hesketh, and Pring studied low-cost caregiver training for feeding difficulties in children with cerebral palsy in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Their findings were published in Child Care Health Dev in 2012. 29. Zuurmond, O’Banion, Gladstone, Carsamar, Kerac, and Baltussen evaluated the impact of a community-based parent training program for children with cerebral palsy in Ghana. Their 2018 study in PLoS One highlights the program’s effectiveness. 30. Teixeira, Paiva, Couto, Oliveira, and Wolter examined the feelings of HIV-positive women regarding the inability to breastfeed. Their findings were published in Rev Baiana Enfermagem in 2017. 31. Kodish, Bio, Oemcke, Conteh, Beaulière, and Pyne-Bailey studied the impact of the Ebola virus disease outbreak on nutrition in Sierra Leone. Their 2019 study in PLoS Negl Trop Dis provides a framework for improving future response strategies. 32. Zihlmann, Alvarenga, and Casseb explored reproductive decisions among individuals living with HTLV-1. Their findings were published in Infect Dis Ther in 2013. 33. Zihlmann, Mazzaia, and De Alvarenga examined the meanings of breastfeeding interruption due to HTLV-1 infection. Their findings were published in Acta Paulista Enfermagem in 2017. 34. Kodish, Rohner, Beaulière, Daffe, Ayoya, and Wirth analyzed the implications of the Ebola outbreak in Guinea for health and nutrition-related responses. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2018. 35. Oni, Djossou, Joubert, and Heraud studied awareness of HTLV-1 transmission through breastfeeding among HTLV-positive women in French Guiana. Their findings were published in Trans R Soc Trop Med Hyg in 2006. 36. Nawa, Kogaki, Takahashi, Ishida, Baden, and Katsuragi analyzed public concerns about influenza vaccinations in Japan using online data mining. Their findings were published in Vaccine in 2016. 37. Abu-Rish, Elayeh, and Browning examined physicians’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding Zika virus infection in Jordan. Their findings were published in J Infect Dev Ctries in 2019. 38. WHO and UNICEF published the Global Breastfeeding Scorecard in 2019, emphasizing the need for increased commitment to breastfeeding through funding, policies, and programs.
